newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela weighs 3 more Orinoco oil deals - sources.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela weighs 3 more Orinoco oil deals - sources.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) is weighing three more multibillion-dollar Orinoco crude oil ventures to add to six already under varying stages of development, company sources said on Thursday.

One of the new ventures would involve PDVSA subsidiary Lagoven with British Petroleum Co Plc. A second would team Lagoven with Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Texaco Inc. The third would involve PDVSA's Corpoven subsidiary with Amerada Hess Corp in the third, they said.

All three are in the early stages of negotiation, but would probably involve investments of $2 billion to $3 billion each in production and upgrading facilities to turn the Orinoco's extra-heavy crude into something resembling conventional oil.

The Orinoco Belt has great attractions for the world's major oil companies because of its enormous untapped reserves. PDVSA estimates 270 billion barrels of recoverable oil, compared with Venezuela's conventional proven oil reserves of 73 billion.

PDVSA has already signed five deals with various major companies and is close to signing a sixth with Coastal Corp. The most advanced of the deals, between PDVSA subsidiary Maraven and Conoco, recently received an investment rating from Standard & Poor's credit rating agency.
The six projects are worth $17 billion, a figure that could rise to $25 billion with three more.
